title: URL Shortener Service with Click Analytics

functional_requirements.statement: A client can submit a long URL and receive a newly created short link identified by a short code.
functional_requirements.source_quote: Create a short link from a long URL

functional_requirements.statement: Requesting an existing short code redirects the client to the original long URL associated with that short code.
functional_requirements.source_quote: redirect from the short code to the original URL

functional_requirements.statement: The redirect response uses HTTP status 302 (temporary redirect).
functional_requirements.source_quote: Use a temporary redirect (302) so every click reaches the service and is counted.

functional_requirements.statement: A client can retrieve the details of an existing short link by its short code.
The service keeps a total click count for each short link, incremented by one on each successful redirect.
functional_requirements.source_quote: Total click count per short link

functional_requirements.statement: The service records the timestamp of the most recent click (successful redirect) for each short link.
functional_requirements.source_quote: plus the timestamp of the last click

functional_requirements.statement: A client can retrieve a short link's analytics, consisting of the total click count and the last-click timestamp, through a separate per-link API call.
functional_requirements.source_quote: exposed via an API call for that link

functional_requirements.statement: Short codes are always generated by the service; clients cannot supply a custom alias.
functional_requirements.source_quote: Create a short link from a long URL

functional_requirements.statement: Each create submission produces a new, independent short link with its own short code and click count, even when the same long URL was submitted before.
functional_requirements.source_quote: Create a short link from a long URL

functional_requirements.statement: Only absolute http or https URLs are accepted when creating a short link; any other value is rejected with a client error (4xx) response and no short link is created.
functional_requirements.source_quote: Create a short link from a long URL

functional_requirements.statement: A short link's details include the short code, the original long URL and the creation timestamp.
The redirect, details and analytics calls return 404 Not Found for a short code that does not exist.
functional_requirements.source_quote: redirect from the short code to the original URL

functional_requirements.statement: For a short link that has never been clicked, analytics report a click count of 0 and a null or absent last-click timestamp.
functional_requirements.source_quote: Total click count per short link, plus the timestamp of the last click

functional_requirements.statement: Every successful redirect counts as exactly one click, including repeat clicks from the same client, with no de-duplication or bot filtering.
functional_requirements.source_quote: so every click reaches the service and is counted

functional_requirements.statement: All operations (create, redirect, details, analytics) can be called without authentication.
functional_requirements.source_quote: Create a short link from a long URL, redirect from the short code to the original URL, and retrieve a short link's details

acceptance_criteria.given: The service is running
acceptance_criteria.when: A client submits a create request with the long URL https://example.com/some/long/path
acceptance_criteria.then: The response has a 2xx status and its body contains a non-empty short code

acceptance_criteria.given: A short link was just created for https://example.com/some/long/path
acceptance_criteria.when: The client requests the details of the returned short code
acceptance_criteria.then: The response has status 200 and the original URL equals https://example.com/some/long/path

acceptance_criteria.given: A short link exists for https://example.com/target
acceptance_criteria.when: A client requests the redirect for its short code without following redirects
acceptance_criteria.then: The response Location header equals https://example.com/target

acceptance_criteria.given: A short link exists for https://example.com/target
acceptance_criteria.when: A client requests the redirect for its short code without following redirects
acceptance_criteria.then: The response status code is exactly 302

acceptance_criteria.given: A short link exists with short code S
acceptance_criteria.when: A client requests the details for short code S
acceptance_criteria.then: The response has status 200 and the returned short code equals S

acceptance_criteria.given: A newly created short link with 0 clicks
acceptance_criteria.when: A client performs the redirect 3 times and then requests the link's analytics
acceptance_criteria.then: The analytics response reports a total click count of 3

acceptance_criteria.given: Two short links A and B exist, each with 0 clicks
acceptance_criteria.when: A client performs the redirect for A twice and for B once, then requests analytics for both
acceptance_criteria.then: Analytics report 2 clicks for A and 1 click for B

acceptance_criteria.given: A newly created short link
acceptance_criteria.when: A client records time T1, performs one redirect, records time T2, and requests the link's analytics
acceptance_criteria.then: The last-click timestamp is present and is greater than or equal to T1 and less than or equal to T2

acceptance_criteria.given: A short link that has been clicked once with last-click timestamp L1
acceptance_criteria.when: A client performs another redirect after L1 and requests the analytics again
acceptance_criteria.then: The new last-click timestamp is later than L1

acceptance_criteria.given: A short link exists with short code S that has been clicked once
acceptance_criteria.when: A client calls the analytics operation for short code S
acceptance_criteria.then: The response has status 200 and contains a total click count of 1 and a non-null last-click timestamp

acceptance_criteria.given: The service is running
acceptance_criteria.when: A client creates two short links for different long URLs
acceptance_criteria.then: Both responses contain service-generated short codes and the two short codes are different

acceptance_criteria.given: The service is running
acceptance_criteria.when: A client submits the same long URL https://example.com/dup in two separate create requests
acceptance_criteria.then: The two responses contain different short codes

acceptance_criteria.given: Two short links A and B were created for the same long URL
acceptance_criteria.when: A client performs the redirect for A once and then requests analytics for A and B
acceptance_criteria.then: Analytics report 1 click for A and 0 clicks for B

acceptance_criteria.given: The service is running
acceptance_criteria.when: A client submits a create request with the value ftp://example.com/file
acceptance_criteria.then: The response status is in the 4xx range and no short code is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: The service is running
acceptance_criteria.when: A client submits a create request with the relative value /just/a/path
acceptance_criteria.then: The response status is in the 4xx range and no short code is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: The service is running
acceptance_criteria.when: A client submits a create request with http://example.com
acceptance_criteria.then: The response has a 2xx status and contains a short code

acceptance_criteria.given: A client recorded time T1, created a short link for https://example.com/details, and recorded time T2
acceptance_criteria.when: The client requests the details for the returned short code
acceptance_criteria.then: The response contains the short code, the original URL https://example.com/details, and a creation timestamp between T1 and T2 inclusive

acceptance_criteria.given: No short link exists with short code doesnotexist123
acceptance_criteria.when: A client requests the redirect for doesnotexist123
acceptance_criteria.then: The response status is 404

acceptance_criteria.given: No short link exists with short code doesnotexist123
acceptance_criteria.when: A client requests the details for doesnotexist123
acceptance_criteria.then: The response status is 404

acceptance_criteria.given: No short link exists with short code doesnotexist123
acceptance_criteria.when: A client requests the analytics for doesnotexist123
acceptance_criteria.then: The response status is 404

acceptance_criteria.given: A short link was just created and never redirected
acceptance_criteria.when: A client requests its analytics
acceptance_criteria.then: The response reports a click count of 0 and the last-click timestamp is null or absent

acceptance_criteria.given: A newly created short link with 0 clicks
acceptance_criteria.when: The same client performs the redirect 5 times in succession with identical request headers and then requests analytics
acceptance_criteria.then: The analytics response reports a click count of 5

acceptance_criteria.given: A short link with 0 clicks and a nonexistent short code doesnotexist123
acceptance_criteria.when: A client requests the redirect for doesnotexist123 and then requests analytics for the existing link
acceptance_criteria.then: The existing link's click count remains 0

acceptance_criteria.given: The service is running
acceptance_criteria.when: A client sends create, redirect, details and analytics requests without any credentials or authorization header
acceptance_criteria.then: None of the responses has status 401 or 403, and each succeeds with its expected status (2xx for create, 302 for redirect, 200 for details and analytics)

assumptions.text: Short codes are always generated by the service; custom aliases are not supported (Q-1 default).
Submitting the same long URL more than once creates a new, independent short link each time (Q-2 default).
Only absolute http/https URLs are accepted on create; anything else is rejected with a client error (Q-3 default).
Details include the short code, the original URL and the creation timestamp; analytics (total clicks and last-click timestamp) are returned by a separate per-link call (Q-4 default).
Redirect, details and analytics calls return 404 Not Found for unknown short codes (Q-5 default).
A never-clicked link reports a click count of 0 and a null/absent last-click timestamp (Q-6 default).
Every successful redirect counts as one click, with no de-duplication or bot filtering (Q-7 default).
No authentication is required; all operations are public (Q-8 default).
Per C-1, 'reliability features' maps to no catalog entry, so no non-functional requirement is included until the user selects one or more catalog entries.

out_of_scope: Rate limiting, contract input validation and Prometheus metrics NFRs (C-1 answered 'none')
Uptime, failover and durability guarantees (cannot be built or validated per C-1)
Updating or deleting short links (not requested)
Per-click analytics beyond total count and last-click timestamp, such as referrer, geography or user agent (not requested)

clarifications.question: Which catalog capability does 'reliability features' refer to: per-client rate limiting on write endpoints (RL-BASIC), contract-based input validation with problem+json errors (SEC-INPUT), Prometheus request metrics at /metrics (OBS-METRICS), or none? Other reliability concerns, such as uptime, failover or durability guarantees, cannot be built or validated.
clarifications.answer: none (no NFR is added until the user picks one or more catalog entries)

clarifications.question: Which operations make up the 'core APIs'?
clarifications.answer: Create a short link from a long URL, redirect from the short code to the original URL, and retrieve a short link's details

clarifications.question: What should 'analytics' capture and expose for each short link?
clarifications.answer: Total click count per short link, plus the timestamp of the last click, exposed via an API call for that link

clarifications.question: Which HTTP redirect status should the redirect use: temporary (302/307) or permanent (301/308)?
clarifications.answer: Use a temporary redirect (302) so every click reaches the service and is counted.
